title: M1: Model language versions, provenance and editorial scope
description:
As an editor, I want each content item to have a stable identity and versioned language renditions, so source relationships, authorship and approvals remain accurate.

Define supported locales and a publication default; original writing language per item; source version and content hash for each rendition; status and history for generated, edited and approved text; translation versus explicitly adapted content; human edit protection. Apply to Reference, Item/Story, SemanticNode/Concept, NewsroomSection and public page metadata, retaining one shared evidence graph, concept identity and lifecycle. Include language-specific section guidance and editorial policy overlays while keeping canonical mission and doctrine in backend data. Decide how original language differs from a later editorial source language.

Acceptance: original and translated versions remain linked to the same item; a localized concept name and aliases resolve to the shared concept; provenance distinguishes drafted, translated, edited and approved actions for the exact rendition; correcting or changing a source marks dependent renditions stale without losing manual edits. Gherkin scenarios and tests cover identity, version transitions and backward compatibility of existing single-language sites.
